hero.subtitle: How we protect your personal data — OnLaw Office, Law Firm of Av. Orjon Nallbati

privacyTab.introText: This notice explains how OnLaw Office collects, uses and protects your personal data when you visit onlawoffice.com, when you contact us through the site, and when you use the firm's internal platform, in accordance with Law No. 124/2024 "On the protection of personal data".

controller.title: Who are we? (Data Controller)
controller.text: The controller of personal data is:
controller.contactNote: For any questions regarding the processing of your personal data, you may contact us at the email address above.

dataCollected.title: What data do we collect?
dataCollected.intro: When you use the site or the platform, we may collect the following categories of data:
dataCollected.contactFormTitle: a) Data from the contact form:
technicalItems: Date and time of the visit
While the page loads, your browser requests fonts from Google Fonts and the map from Google Maps, which transmits your IP address to Google LLC
dataCollected.noSensitive: Please do not send sensitive data through the contact form: health information, data on criminal proceedings, confidential documents or data about other people. Describe the matter in general terms; if the engagement proceeds, we will collect such data later through a protected channel and with the appropriate notice. Sensitive data you nevertheless send voluntarily is processed only to assess your request, on the basis of article 9 of Law 124/2024, and deleted if the engagement does not proceed.
dataCollected.platformTitle: c) Internal platform data (only for accounts opened by invitation):
platformItems: Password — stored only in hashed form, never in plain text
Licence number and bar association, where provided
Professional data the user records in the platform (cases, clients, documents, deadlines)
dataCollected.platformNote: The platform is a working tool of the firm: accounts are opened only by invitation from OnLaw Office and used by its collaborators. It is not a service open to the public.

purpose.title: Why do we process data and on what legal basis?
purpose.intro: Your data is processed for the following purposes:

contactResponse.title: Responding to your request (Contact form)
contactResponse.text: Legal basis: pre-contractual steps taken at your request, or your consent (article 7, Law 124/2024).

technicalFunction.title: Technical operation of the website
technicalFunction.text: Legal basis: the controller's legitimate interest in the technical operation and security of the site (article 7, Law 124/2024).

legalObligation.title: Fulfilment of legal obligations
legalObligation.text: Legal basis: the controller's legal obligation (article 7, Law 124/2024), such as keeping records under tax or archiving legislation.

platformAccount.title: Account on the internal platform
platformAccount.text: Legal basis: performance of the employment or collaboration relationship with OnLaw Office, and the controller's legitimate interest in system security (article 7, Law 124/2024). Account data is used only for identification, access control and security.

retention.title: How long do we keep data?
retention.intro: We apply the principle of storage limitation (article 6, Law 124/2024):

items.label: Contact data:
items.text: Kept until the exchange with you ends and no longer than 12 months after the last contact, unless a contractual relationship is established. The copy of the message held by the form provider (Formspree) is deleted automatically after 30 days.

items.label: Technical data (logs):
items.text: Kept for up to 90 days, solely for technical security.

items.label: Platform accounts:
items.text: Kept while the account is active and for up to 12 months after it is closed; closure can be requested at any time by email.

items.label: Legal/contractual records:
items.text: Kept for the statutory periods in force (up to 10 years under tax legislation).

retention.afterExpiry: After the expiry of the retention period, data is deleted or anonymised.

sharing.title: With whom do we share data?
sharing.intro: Your personal data is not sold, traded or shared with third parties for marketing purposes.
sharing.availableTo: They may be made available only to processors acting on our instructions under a contract pursuant to article 26 of Law 124/2024, and to public authorities where the law requires it:

items.label: Vercel Inc. (USA)
items.text: — hosting and delivery of the site; processes the technical data of each visit.

items.label: Supabase Inc.
items.text: — database and document storage for the platform; servers located in Frankfurt (EU).

items.label: Formspree Inc. (USA)
items.text: — the service that forwards contact-form messages to our email and stores them for up to 30 days.

items.label: Google LLC (USA)
items.text: — fonts (Google Fonts) and the map (Google Maps) loaded on the site; receives your IP address when the page loads.

items.label: Public authorities
items.text: — only where required by law or by court order.

sharing.formNote: The contact form runs on Formspree: your message reaches us by email and a copy is held temporarily by Formspree (up to 30 days), after which it is deleted automatically. We use it for no other purpose and do not share it with third parties.

transfers.title: Is data transferred outside Albania?
transfers.text1: The platform database is located within the European Union (Frankfurt). For site hosting, the contact form and Google services, data is also processed in the United States of America.
transfers.text2: In the absence of an adequacy decision by the Commissioner for that country, the transfer relies on the appropriate safeguards provided for in articles 39–41 of Law 124/2024: our processing agreements with these providers include standard contractual clauses for data protection. Copies of the relevant documents can be requested at our email address.

rights.title: What are your rights?
rights.intro: Under articles 13–20 of Law 124/2024 you have the following rights:

items.label: Right to information
items.text: (article 13) — to be informed about the processing

items.label: Right of access
items.text: (article 14) — to obtain a copy of your data

items.label: Right to rectification and erasure
items.text: (article 15) — to correct inaccurate data or request its deletion

items.label: Right to be forgotten
items.text: (article 16) — to request deletion also from parties with whom the data was shared

items.label: Right to data portability
items.text: (article 18) — to receive your data in a readable electronic format

items.label: Right to withdraw consent
items.text: — at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of prior processing

rights.exerciseText: Send your request by email to {email}. We will respond within 30 days.

complaint.title: Right to complain to the Commissioner
complaint.intro: If you consider that your rights have been infringed, you may lodge a complaint with the Commissioner (article 86, Law 124/2024):
complaint.boxTitle: Commissioner for the Right to Information and Personal Data Protection
complaint.legalRemedy: Under article 88 of Law 124/2024 you are also entitled to compensation for damage suffered as a result of unlawful processing.

automated.title: Are automated decisions made?
automated.text: No. OnLaw Office does not use any automated decision-making or profiling system (article 20, Law 124/2024) in relation to site visitors, clients or platform users.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.text: This policy may be updated from time to time to reflect legal changes or changes in our practice. The updated version will be published on this page with the date of update. We encourage you to review it periodically.

cookieTab.introText: This policy explains how the website onlawoffice.com uses cookies — small text files stored on your device when you visit our website.

whatAreCookies.title: What are cookies?
whatAreCookies.text1: Cookies are small text files that websites store on your device (computer, phone, tablet). They help the website function properly, save your preferences and provide a better browsing experience.
whatAreCookies.text2: Cookies do not contain viruses and cannot access other information on your device.

whichCookies.title: Which cookies do we use?
whichCookies.intro: The public site onlawoffice.com sets no cookies. Technical cookies are set only when you sign in to the internal platform (/app), to keep your session open and protect forms against attacks:

cookies.name: __Secure-next-auth.session-token
cookies.duration: Up to 30 days or until sign-out

cookies.name: __Host-next-auth.csrf-token
cookies.purpose: Protection of platform forms against CSRF attacks

cookies.name: __Secure-next-auth.callback-url
cookies.purpose: Return to the right page after sign-in

whichCookies.noAnalyticsText: We do not use Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel or any other tracking tool. Your browsing on our website is not tracked for profiling or advertising purposes.
whichCookies.localStorageNote: The cookie notice sets no cookie: when you dismiss it, your browser stores locally (localStorage) only the entry "cookie-consent", so the notice is not shown again. This entry contains no personal data and is not sent to anyone.

legalBasis.title: Legal basis for cookies
legalBasis.text1: Technical (essential) cookies do not require your consent, as they are necessary for the basic functioning of the website.
legalBasis.text2: Legal basis: Legitimate interest of the controller (Article 7, letter "dh", Law 124/2024) to ensure the technical operation and security of the website.
legalBasis.text3: If in the future we decide to use analytics or marketing cookies, we will update this policy and request your explicit consent before activating them.

manageCookies.title: How to manage cookies?
manageCookies.intro: You can manage or delete cookies through your browser settings:
manageCookies.warning: Warning: Disabling technical cookies may affect the website's functionality, such as the ability to use the contact form.

contactFooter.title: Questions about your data?
contactFooter.text: Contact us for any matter related to privacy and personal data protection.
